heard: A dead star missed a single heartbeat in deep space. This is the Vela pulsar, formed in a massive supernova about 10,000 years ago. Roughly 1,000 light years away, it rotates 11 times every single second. In 2016, astronomers caught a terrifying anomaly live for the very first time. Right as the star glitched, it skipped a pulse entirely, going completely silent. This violent hiccup took five seconds to accelerate the star's rotation. The pulsar's faster liquid core suddenly gripped its outer crust, transferring energy. This engine emits radiation jets reaching 20 tera-electron volts of extreme energy. This cosmic glitch is why a dead star just missed a heartbeat.
